model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^4 (with tick marks at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 40% to 65%, with tick marks every 5 percentage points. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black circles), MEND (brown diamonds), FT (blue triangles), MEMIT (purple diamonds), IKE (red triangles), and ROME (green squares). The ROME method shows the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, starting at approximately 51% and increasing to about 66% at 10^3. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, both starting near 44% and rising to about 54% and 56%, respectively, at 10^3. IKE starts at around 43% and increases to about 49% at 10^3. FT begins at approximately 40% and reaches about 47% at 10^3. Base starts at 39% and rises to about 44% at 10^3, showing the smallest improvement. All lines show a general upward trend with increasing co-occurrence number, though the rate of increase varies by method.
